known_regressions: Observed, not fixed: the Harness empty state scrolls under the composer at 900px, so the third starter card sits below the fold in the refreshed capture. It is the pane's own focusable scroll region (`.harness-stream { overflow-y: auto }`), not a clip, and fixing the fold would be a pane layout change with its own evidence burden.
22 capture sets carry no `index.json`: their captures cannot be shown to be the bytes their walk produced, only that they exist and that their theme is what their name claims.
The published set has no narrow variant. Narrow coverage comes from `polish`, `responsive`, `uiux-p5-05` and `screenshots/p4-01-narrow-dark` (420x1200), which the review counts under their own sets.

Pre-existing and not this story's: the Python 3.12 CI job failed once on `tests/test_trusted_transformations.py::test_http_endpoints_and_standalone_studio_bundle_parity` (`assert eval_json["ab_gate_passed"] is True`). That gate compares `benefit_justifies_cost`, which includes `overhead_med <= TT_MAX_OVERHEAD_MS_CEILING` measured in wall-clock milliseconds, so a busy runner can fail it; the same test passed in the 3.11 and 3.13 jobs and eight local runs, and this story touches no transformation code. The job was re-run by pushing the ledger edit - not by relaxing the test.
decisions: The published set was re-shot rather than re-described. A review that leaves the README showing a pane the tree no longer draws has reviewed nothing.

The dark variant was photographed into `docs/media/uiux-p6-03/after-dark`, not into the published directory: `manifest.json` defines one published set, and a second one would silently change what the README's images promise.
The replaced set is the story's own before. It comes from `git show` at cee9159 with recomputed checksums, so the before/after is two captures of the same six panes rather than a paragraph.

Theme is checked in the pixels, not in the filename. `identify` median luminance separates the program's dark captures (0.09-0.17) from its light ones (0.52-0.97) with a wide gap; thresholds that split the gap cannot be tuned to one set.
A set with no review entry fails `--check`. The review is data, not an appendix: the next capture cannot ship without someone writing down what it shows.

A missing `index.json` is an observation, not a finding. Twenty-two sets were produced by walks that write no index; that weakens the evidence (no recorded capture time or checksum) but it is not a false claim, and the artifact says so per set instead of failing the program on history.
tracking.handoff_note: Re-run `python3 scripts/uiux_screenshot_review.py` after adding or re-shooting any capture: a new set with no entry in `REVIEWS` fails `--check`, which is the point. The published set is re-shot with `node scripts/capture_screenshots.mjs` against `scripts/demo_tour.py --serve`; `validate_screenshots.py` still owns that set, and this review does not replace it.

The 11 distinct read-only commands the pages instruct are executed by `tests/test_uiux_docs_verification.py` with exit-code assertions - `demo_tour.py` (default, `--check`, `--json`), `validate_screenshots.py`, `check_frontend_syntax.py`, `validate_docs.py`, `smoke_local.py`, `pytest -q tests/test_onboarding_preflight.py`, `ruff check .`, `mypy` - via this environment's interpreter, since the pages say `python` as an activated-venv shorthand. 18 tests, all pass; nothing that writes, installs, starts a server or rewrites a tracked generated file is executed.

Negative paths covered without touching the tree: a page that is missing is read as empty (a claim then fails), an unclassified command is a finding (the check exits 1), and a command whose kind is `runs` but which appears in the forbidden-token list fails the policy test.

decisions: A documentation page is verified by executing what it instructs, not by reading it: `runs` commands are executed by the test, and every other command must carry a stated reason, so silence about a new command is a finding.

The pages say `python` because they assume an activated virtualenv; the test substitutes this environment's interpreter rather than rewriting the docs, and says so in the test module's docstring. The command's meaning is unchanged.

No UI change was made for a P2 story whose subject is documentation: adding a docs-only badge or a link to the verification page inside the app would be a UI change nobody asked for, and the docs index and program table carry the pointer instead.

The generator reads the same five pages `scripts/validate_docs.py` already renders, rather than widening that script: link and anchor checking belongs to one owner, and command execution belongs to a test that can assert exit codes.

stories.title: Release gate and handover report
stories.description: Incrementally implement release gate and handover report using current code as authoritative baseline.
stories.current_behavior: Measured, not read. Thirty-nine stories had produced thirty-nine artifacts, each with its own `--check` mode, and nothing ran them together: a reader asking whether the program was finished had to run thirty-seven generators by hand and hold the results in their head, and nothing anywhere stated which of the program's own phase gates was met, which acceptance criterion each artifact answered, or what remained imperfect. The ledger's `release_gates` sentences were prose, and no file existed that a reviewer could read instead of forty pull requests.
stories.target_behavior: One command runs every artifact check on the tree and records each exit code and summary line, then computes the seven phase gates from the stories and the checks rather than asserting them, maps the five acceptance criteria to the artifact or CI job that answers each, carries every recorded known regression with the story that recorded it, names the suites it deliberately does not run, and emits a handover report: what changed, what held, how to verify in five minutes, and what is not claimed. A failed check unmeets the gate it proves; a counter that disagrees with its stories is a finding.

No console errors on tested journeys

stories.rollback_strategy: Revert only this story commit; do not modify user workspace data or durable state schemas.
stories.agent_prompt: Implement UIUX-P6-05 (Release gate and handover report). Verify dependencies, pin HEAD, inventory impacted controls and API routes, preserve all current behavior, make a small compatible change, execute targeted and baseline tests, record screenshots, and mark done only with passing evidence. Never invent a test result.

evidence: Before, measured: 39 artifacts, 19 generators with `--check` modes, and no single command that ran them. `release_gates` was seven sentences of prose; nothing computed whether a gate was met, nothing mapped the five acceptance criteria to evidence, and the 45 recorded known regressions were scattered across 39 story entries.

After: `python scripts/uiux_release_gate.py` runs all 37 artifact checks in the documented order, records each exit code and its summary line, and reports `37/37 checks, 7/7 gates, 0 findings`. `--check` compares the JSON, the gate page and the handover against a fresh run, so a drifted artifact fails the release gate as well as its own check.

The seven phase gates are computed, not asserted: each is met only when every story in that phase is `done` and every generator that phase owns exits 0. A test breaks one P0-06 check in the check list and asserts the P0 gate flips to unmet.

The gate's bookkeeping checks close the ways a ledger can lie: counters that disagree with the stories, a phase counter that disagrees with its members, a `done` story without a 40-hex commit sha, and a `done` story without evidence are each a finding, and each has its own falsifying test.

The five acceptance criteria are mapped to the artifact or CI job that answers each - control inventory plus preservation e2e plus `Browser safety regressions`; the browser walks' console assertions; the overlay/shortcut inventory plus the keyboard walks; the adversarial and presentation inventories; 240 reviewed captures - and the artifact records that the verdict belongs to the reviewer, not to this script.

Honesty about coverage: `not_run` names the full pytest matrix, the browser suites, a new screenshot capture and the acceptance verdict itself, each with the reason. The gate carries no clock, so two runs agree and `--check` is meaningful.

Handover: `docs/uiux-2-0-handover.md` is generated from the same payload - six paragraphs on what changed, three on what held (21 capabilities, no route removed, no new dependency, 12 mapped refusals), five commands to verify in five minutes, where the evidence lives, what is not claimed, and all 45 known regressions with the story that recorded each.

The gate proved itself on its first real use: running it against the committed tree turned both of the defects above from invisible into failing tests. `scripts/uiux_screenshot_review.py --check` now passes with and without ImageMagick, and `tests/test_uiux_release_gate.py` asserts that a passing check carries no words while a failing one carries its output.

Closed after the gate: `record_perf(..., demo: bool = False)` returns before writing, all four call sites pass the flag from the usage line that carries it, and `studio.py` is rebuilt from `app.py` (`Build studio.py: 3,498,647 bytes`, identical on a second run). The release gate now carries `resolved_regressions` and prints them in both documents, and it fails closed if the ledger's recorded wording moves out from under a closure claim (`resolution-reference`), or if the proof test is missing.

The new test module is mapped in `tests/test_scopes.json` under `storage.history`, so the scoped selector knows which area it belongs to; `tests/test_scoped_tests.py` fails when a module is unmapped, and it would have failed here without that line.

The reproducibility failure was diagnosed from the run's annotations and reproduced locally: `python scripts/generate_subsystem_inventory.py` rewrote `docs/subsystem-dependency-inventory.md` after the `app.py` change, and `--check` on that script is not a check - it exits 0 and rewrites. Both generators that behave this way are now listed in the gate (`GENERATED_WITHOUT_CHECK`), executed on every run, and byte-compared; the gate restores the file before it reports, so `--check` never repairs the tree it is inspecting.

The ceiling was measured, not guessed: five local suite runs put the transform's median cost at 2.08-2.32 ms against a baseline operation of 2.79 ms, roughly 0.75x, so a runner about 20x slower than this one crosses 50 ms while the ratio does not move. `overhead_allowance_ms` and `overhead_within_allowance` are now reported per scenario, so a failure names which rule it broke, and the ratio is a constant (`TT_OVERHEAD_BASELINE_RATIO`) with its reasoning beside it.
test_results: `.venv/bin/python scripts/uiux_release_gate.py --check` -> `release gate OK: 37/37 artifact checks pass, 7/7 phase gates met, 45 known regressions, 0 findings`, exit 0.

`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_uiux_release_gate.py` -> 15 tests, all pass, exit 0. The module-scoped fixture runs the thirty-seven checks once; the negative tests work on deep copies of the ledger.

`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` (whole suite, 3.11.9, Linux x86_64) -> `2600 passed, 28 skipped, 1 warning in 440.28s`, exit 0. The run used the full history: this checkout was unshallowed (`git fetch --unshallow`) so the three ancestor assertions that cannot run in a shallow clone - `tests/test_baseline.py` and the two in `tests/test_uiux_preservation_signoff.py` - ran here too. The same suite also passed with ImageMagick hidden from `PATH`, the condition CI is in.

`.venv/bin/ruff check .` -> `All checks passed!`; `.venv/bin/python -m mypy` -> 58 source files, no issues; `scripts/check_frontend_syntax.py`, `scripts/validate_docs.py`, `scripts/validate_screenshots.py`, `scripts/demo_tour.py --check` -> exit 0.

`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_uiux_screenshot_review.py` -> 15 passed, including the new `test_the_check_mode_survives_a_machine_without_imagemagick`, which would have failed before this story's fix.

`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_perf_samples_honesty.py` -> 6 passed: no sample for a demo reply, a measured reply still stored, the throughput summary never averaging a demo row, every `record_perf` call site passing the flag (AST walk over `app.py`), the demo usage line still carrying `demo: True`, and the generated bundle carrying the same refusal. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_uiux_release_gate.py` -> 17 passed.

`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_uiux_release_gate.py` -> 19 passed, including `test_a_stale_generated_file_is_a_finding_and_the_tree_is_left_as_it_was`, which appends a line to a generated file, asserts the finding, asserts the file came back byte-identical to the stale version, and restores the true bytes.

`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_trusted_transformations.py` -> 8 passed, including the two new tests: a slow runner (baseline 400 ms, overhead 125 ms) now passes with an allowance of 400 ms where it used to fail, and a transform costing three times the work it wraps still fails, as does one over the floor on a fast machine.
`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` (whole suite, 3.11.9, Linux x86_64, full history) -> `2613 passed, 28 skipped, 1 warning in 505.64s`, exit 0, with both closures in place.
visual_evidence: No pixel changed: `static/index.html` and `app.py` are byte-identical to the P6-04 merge, so there is no before/after to take and the 240-capture set stands unchanged.

The program's visual evidence is summarised where a reviewer will look for it: `docs/uiux-2-0-release-gate.md` prints the capture counts (240 files, 27 sets, 27 reviewed) and the gate asserts the artifact that owns them still validates.
decisions: The gate executes the artifacts' own `--check` modes instead of re-deriving their facts: one owner per fact, and a check that runs is worth more than a summary that parses.

It does not run the full test suite or the browser suites. Claiming three interpreters' worth of results from one local run would be exactly the dishonesty this program has been avoiding, and this checkout is shallow, so three ancestor assertions cannot run at all; they are named in `not_run` and in the artifact.
The acceptance verdict stays with the owner and the reviewer: the gate maps each criterion to evidence and prints it, and says in the artifact that the call is not its own.
Known regressions are carried, not resolved. Closing 45 recorded imperfections at the end of a program would be a silently larger change than any story that found them.
Two documents from one payload: the gate page for a reviewer checking the release, the handover for whoever inherits the repository.

`tests/test_uiux_roadmap.py` now permits `next_recommended_story: null`, but only when every story is `done` and no story is active; the assertion it replaces required a story id at all times, which a finished program cannot honestly supply. The relaxation fails closed: a null recommendation with any open story is still an error, and the test says so by name.

The gate found two real defects the moment it ran every check, and both were fixed here rather than worked around. First, `scripts/uiux_screenshot_review.py --check` compared its generated page against the committed page character for character, so it failed on any machine without ImageMagick `identify` (CI has none) while passing on one that has it: the page is now compared with the committed artifact's own rendering, the pixel pass reports that it did not run, and a test monkeypatches the measurement away to keep it that way. Second, the gate itself copied each passing check's last printed line into its artifact, which made the artifact differ between two machines that agreed on the tree - one of those lines names whether ImageMagick is installed. A passing check now contributes only its exit code; a failing one contributes what it said, in the finding.

The first item of the backlog the handover named is closed, as maintenance rather than as a new story: the demo path no longer writes its invented throughput figures (29.5 / 42.1 tok/s, 155 prefill, 0.32 s) into `perf_samples`. The flag already travelled with the usage line and every surface already declined to draw it; `record_perf` now declines to store it too, because a fabricated row in the table the throughput card averages is indistinguishable from a measured one. The ledger's own story entries are not rewritten - the recorded line stays as history - and the gate states which carried lines no longer stand, with the test that proves it.

CI caught what this gate did not, and the gap is closed: changing `app.py` also moves `docs/subsystem-dependency-inventory.md`, whose generator ignores `--check` and rewrites its output unconditionally, so the committed bytes went stale and `Verify generated artifacts are reproducible` failed on two of three interpreters. The gate now runs both such generators, compares the bytes and restores the file it found, so a stale generated file is a release-gate finding rather than a CI surprise. The handoff note says the same thing in one sentence for the next session.

Second backlog item closed, and it was the only recurring red run: the A/B gate compared a transform's median cost to an absolute 50 ms, so a loaded runner failed it while the same commit passed on a laptop. The allowance is now `max(50 ms, 1.0 x the baseline operation's median latency)`: the transform runs inside the operation it qualifies, so its cost is judged against that operation's cost on the machine measuring it. The floor keeps fast machines from failing on noise, and the ratio can only relax it - a transform that costs three times the work it wraps still fails, which is a test.
tracking.handoff_note: The program is complete at 40/40 and one carried regression is now closed (the demo path's fabricated throughput no longer reaches `perf_samples`); the release gate lists both the 45 recorded lines and the one that no longer stands, with proof. What a next session should know: the ledger, the manifest and the sign-off share one pin (`73bc5e417c15`, approved by the owner as UIUX-P0-06), so any change to a pinned file means regenerating the manifest and the sign-off in the same commit; changing `app.py` also moves `docs/route-security-matrix.md` and `docs/subsystem-dependency-inventory.md`, whose generators ignore `--check`, so regenerate those two by hand and let the gate prove the bytes; `python3 scripts/uiux_release_gate.py --check` is the single command that proves the whole program still holds; and the remaining known regressions are the honest backlog, not a blocker.

release_gates.P0: Inventory and preservation baseline recorded: pinned HEAD, every tab and control enumerated, frontend handler to API route map, backend authorization trace, baseline screenshots and test results, owner-approved preservation matrix. No redesign before this.
release_gates.P1: Design tokens, navigation shell, shared status/evidence components and accessible overlays exist with no route or capability change and with keyboard coverage.
release_gates.P2: Start and Chat journeys are usable end to end, including empty, loading, streaming, error and recovery states, with an explicit Chat-to-Harness handoff.
release_gates.P3: Harness and Pipeline surface durable task state, approvals, diffs, artifacts and pause/cancel/resume/recovery without inventing client-side state.
release_gates.P4: Council and Compare present participants, stages, disagreement and measured provenance without collapsing the two workflows into one.
release_gates.P5: Cross-tab consistency and accessibility/responsive regression are demonstrated: keyboard walks, screen-reader labels, touch targets, bounded SSE rendering.
release_gates.P6: Automated preservation end-to-end tests, adversarial permission/recovery UI tests, full screenshot review, README/onboarding verification and a release gate with a handover report.

readme_contract.rule: README describes only verified behaviour. A UI/UX story that changes what a user can do updates the affected section in the same pull request; a story that changes nothing user-visible says so in its tracking block instead of touching the README.
forbidden: presenting a planned story, mockup, screenshot of a mock or an unverified design as shipped
claiming accessibility conformance from intent rather than a keyboard/screen-reader walk that was executed
claiming performance numbers that were not measured on a named machine
